end.summary:
• Practised placing BCE and CE dates on a timeline.
• Aarav correctly ordered 3000 BCE, 500 BCE, 100 CE, and 1947 CE.
• Discussed archaeological remains, inscriptions, texts, and oral traditions as historical sources.
• Aarav continued to say that written sources should be fully believed; this was not corrected by the end.
end.parentNote: Asha practised the timeline method of counting BCE years backwards towards 1 BCE and placing CE dates to the right; Aarav used this to order four dates correctly. They also discussed checking information across different sources, but the mix-up that one written source tells the whole truth remained at the end. At home, ask Aarav to compare a short written account with an object, image, or oral account and note one way the sources agree or differ.
